deed: האחים ביילסקי הקימו קהילה ביער והצילו יותר מ-1,200 יהודים
title: The Bielski brothers fled to the forest, took in every Jew who came, and at liberation the group numbered more than 1,200 people

trailer.text: Tuvia Bielski and his brothers, a Jewish farming family from the Novogrudok area, led the Bielski partisans, whose story became the film "Defiance", starring Daniel Craig and Liev Schreiber.
According to Yad Vashem, Tuvia Bielski (1906–1987) was a Jewish partisan commander.
According to USHMM, in 1941 the Germans killed his parents and two of his brothers in the Novogrudok ghetto, and the surviving brothers fled to the forest and formed a partisan group.
According to USHMM, the brothers, led by Tuvia, decided to save as many Jews as possible, although many in the group wanted to keep their numbers small.
According to USHMM, by the summer of 1944 the group had grown to 1,200 people, most of them elderly people, women and children.

glance.label: Founders
glance.value: The brothers Tuvia, Asael and Zus Bielski

glance.label: Beginning
glance.value: After the murder of the parents in the ghetto. According to USHMM the parents were murdered in the Novogrudok ghetto in December 1941, and according to JewishGen they were murdered in the ghetto in August 1941.

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: According to USHMM, among the largest rescues of Jews by Jews

paragraphs.text: According to USHMM, Tuvia Bielski was born in 1906 in Stankiewicze, in western Belorussia.
According to USHMM, the Bielskis were a Jewish farming family in the village, and the brothers knew the region well.
According to Yad Vashem, at the age of 17 Tuvia joined a Zionist pioneering movement.
According to Yad Vashem, in 1928 he was drafted into the Polish army and rose to the rank of corporal.
According to USHMM, between July 1941 and the end of spring 1942 the German authorities killed tens of thousands of Jews in Novogrudok District, which included the cities of Lida and Novogrudok.
According to USHMM, in the Novogrudok ghetto the Germans murdered four thousand Jews, among them the brothers' parents.
According to USHMM, two of their brothers were also murdered there.
According to USHMM, the remaining brothers fled to the forests and formed the nucleus of a partisan detachment.
According to USHMM, the family members chose Tuvia, a Polish army veteran and Zionist activist, to command the group.
According to USHMM, Asael was Tuvia's deputy, and Zus was placed in charge of reconnaissance.
According to USHMM, with the help of non-Jewish Belorussian friends, the brothers were able to acquire weapons.
According to USHMM, Tuvia saw saving the lives of his fellow Jews as his principal mission.
According to USHMM, he told his fighters that lives had to be saved, and that saving a Jew was much more important than killing Germans.
According to Srugim, Tuvia told his men again and again that he would rather have one living Jew than ten dead Germans.
According to USHMM, many in the group argued that they would be safer if they stayed few and did not accept more Jews.
According to USHMM, Tuvia did not waver, and accepted and protected all Jewish refugees, regardless of age or gender.
According to USHMM, in late 1942 a special mission saved more than a hundred Jews from the Iwie ghetto, just as the Germans planned to liquidate it.
According to USHMM, the family of Konstantin Kozlovski, a non-Jew, hid Jews who had escaped from the Novogrudok ghetto, and worked with the partisans to free hundreds of Jews from the ghetto.
According to USHMM, by the end of 1942 the group had grown to more than 300 people.
According to USHMM, by February 1943, 300 Jews were living in the forest as Bielski partisans.
According to USHMM, in August 1943 the Germans began a massive manhunt against Russian, Polish and Jewish partisans in the region.
According to USHMM, the Germans offered a reward of 100,000 Reichsmarks for information leading to the capture of Tuvia Bielski.

According to Yad Vashem, when the area commander ordered Tuvia to reduce his unit to armed single men only and to leave behind the married men, the women and the children, he knew that this was a death sentence for the civilians in his group.
According to Yad Vashem, he refused and retreated into the depths of the forest with the entire group.
According to USHMM, they spent ten days in the swamp, covered in mud, and evaded patrols of Germans and of Belorussian collaborators.

stations.title: A small town in the Naliboki Forest

paragraphs.text: According to USHMM, in December 1943 the group moved to a permanent base in the Naliboki Forest.
According to Srugim, this was not an ordinary partisan battalion but a Jewish community in the forest.
According to USHMM, the camp had workshops of cobblers, tailors, carpenters, leather workers and blacksmiths.
According to JewishGen, the fame of the workshops reached partisans far beyond the Bielski base.
According to USHMM, the forest also had a soap factory, a Turkish bath and butchers.
According to USHMM, the leadership ran a primitive infirmary, a school for the children, a synagogue, and even a courthouse and jail.
According to USHMM, the school built in the camp served more than 50 children.
According to USHMM, a group of musicians performed in the camp at festivals.
According to USHMM, despite the antisemitism in Soviet units, General "Platon" protected the Bielski group.
According to USHMM, Bielski refused Soviet requests to provide an operations unit from among the approximately 150 fighting men in his group.
According to USHMM, the group disabled German trains, blew up rail beds, destroyed bridges and helped Jews escape from ghettos.

stations.title: Liberation: more than a thousand people come out of the forest

paragraphs.text: According to Yad Vashem, in the summer of 1944, with the liberation of the area, Bielski and his people marched to the city of Novogrudok.
According to USHMM, more than 70 percent of the group's members at liberation were women, elderly people and children, who without the group would have perished under the German occupation.
According to JewishGen, no one was turned away.
According to USHMM, about 50 members of the group were killed, an unusually low casualty rate compared with other partisan units and with Jewish groups in the region.
According to USHMM, Tuvia's group was the largest of the Jewish partisan groups.
According to USHMM, today the Bielski partisans are considered one of the largest rescues of Jews by Jews in the history of the Holocaust.

stations.title: After the war: the brothers, the descendants and the memory

paragraphs.text: According to the USHMM, after the war many of the survivors who returned home found others living in their homes, and in many cases the locals who had seized their property were violently antisemitic and refused to discuss returning it.
According to Yad Vashem, Tuvia first returned to Poland.
According to USHMM, in 1945 Tuvia and Zus emigrated with their families to Palestine.
According to USHMM, Tuvia and Zus fought in the Israeli armed forces in the 1948 war, in which the State of Israel was established.
According to Yad Vashem, in 1954 Tuvia settled in the United States with his two surviving brothers.
According to USHMM, Tuvia and Zus worked there in transportation, driving trucks and taxis in New York.
According to Srugim, Avraham Weiner, who worked alongside Tuvia, said that Tuvia was full of national pain and national love for the Jews.
According to JewishGen, none of the Bielskis ever sought recognition or reward for their actions.
According to JewishGen, when Tuvia died in 1987 he was buried on Long Island.
According to JewishGen, a year later, at the urging of surviving partisans in Israel, he was exhumed and buried at Har Hamenuchot in Jerusalem with a hero's funeral.
According to Srugim, he was buried there in a full military ceremony.
According to aboutholocaust, by some estimates the number of descendants of the Bielski group is as high as 10,000.
The story of the Bielski partisans became the film "Defiance".
According to JPEF, the film starred Daniel Craig and Liev Schreiber.
According to JewishGen, the film received mixed reviews and raised questions about the roles various groups played in the war.
According to JewishGen, like other partisan groups in the area, the Bielski men raided villages and took food by force.
According to JewishGen, at times peasants who refused to share their food suffered violence and were even murdered.
According to USHMM, the partisans sometimes robbed peasants at gunpoint, and a few times they killed people who had collaborated with the Germans against them.
According to USHMM, the group attacked Belorussian auxiliary police officials and local farmers suspected of killing Jews.
According to partisan documentation cited by JewishGen, the fighters of the two units claimed to have killed a total of 381 enemy fighters.
According to JewishGen, some members of the unit, but not the brothers themselves, were accused of war crimes.
According to JewishGen, among other things they were accused of alleged involvement in the 1943 Naliboki massacre, in which Soviet partisans killed 129 people.
According to JewishGen, former fighters in the brigade and other historians dispute this, asserting that the partisans arrived in the area only several months later.
According to JewishGen, the Polish Institute of National Remembrance has been investigating the massacre since the early 2000s, and as of April 2009 it had not issued official findings.
According to USHMM, some partisans thought the brothers were overbearing, but Tuvia saw discipline as a condition for the group's survival.
According to JewishGen, there are accounts of inequality in the camp between well-off partisans and poor inhabitants.
According to JewishGen, after the Soviets arrived, the NKVD interrogated the brothers following rumors of loot they had collected during the war.

disagreements.question: When were the brothers' parents killed?

versions.says: USHMM: in December 1941, in the Novogrudok ghetto
JewishGen: in August 1941, in the ghetto

disagreements.question: How many people were in the group at the start?

versions.says: USHMM: about 30 family members and friends
Biography in the USHMM collections: the four brothers and 13 others
Yad Vashem: 17 members, most of them members of the Bielski family
JewishGen: around forty people, and the group grew quickly

disagreements.question: How many workers were in the camp workshops?

versions.says: USHMM: at least 200 people
JewishGen: more than 125 workers

disagreements.question: How many people were in the group at its peak, at liberation?

versions.says: USHMM and Yad Vashem: 1,230 people
JewishGen: 1,236 people
USHMM, in the article on Tuvia Bielski: 1,200 people

disagreements.question: When and where was Asael Bielski killed?

versions.says: USHMM: in February 1945, at the front in East Prussia, as a soldier in the Red Army
Photo caption in the USHMM collections: in the battle of Königsberg in 1944
Yad Vashem: at Königsberg in 1944, as a soldier in the Soviet army
aboutholocaust: in January 1945, after being drafted into the Red Army

disagreements.question: In what year was the film "Defiance" released?

versions.says: JPEF: in 2008
USHMM: in 2009
JewishGen: on January 16, 2009

disagreements.question: When did the Bielski group move to the Naliboki Forest?

versions.says: USHMM Holocaust Encyclopedia: in December 1943, to a permanent base in the forest
USHMM podcast: in the summer of 1943, before the German manhunt, Tuvia led the group to the Naliboki Forest
Yad Vashem: already in the summer of 1943 the Germans carried out a manhunt in the Naliboki Forest, among others against the Bielski group
aboutholocaust: in August 1943 the group was forced to make camp deep in the Naliboki Forest

unknowns.text: The group in the forest formed after the murder of the parents in the Nowogrodek ghetto, but the sources differ on the date of the murder: according to the USHMM, the Germans murdered the parents and two of the brothers in December 1941, and according to JewishGen, the parents and other family members were murdered in August 1941.
The page does not know what the Polish Institute of National Remembrance determined, if anything, after April 2009

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, טוביה ביילסקי (1906–1987) היה מפקד פרטיזנים יהודי.
claims.quote: (1906-1987), Jewish partisan commander. Bielski's family were farmers in Stankiewicze, near Novogrudok.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בדצמבר 1941 הרגו הגרמנים את הוריהם ושניים מאחיהם של האחים ביילסקי בגטו נובוגרודק, ושלושה אחים שורדים הקימו קבוצת פרטיזנים.
claims.quote: After the Germans killed their parents and two brothers in the Nowogrodek ghetto in December 1941, three surviving brothers of the Bielski family

claims.text: לפי USHMM, האחים נמלטו ליערות וייסדו גרעין של פלוגת פרטיזנים שמנתה בתחילה כ-30 בני משפחה וחברים.
claims.quote: They fled to the nearby Zábiedovo and Perelaz forests, where they formed the nucleus of a partisan detachment consisting at first of about 30 family members and friends.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, רבים בקבוצה טענו שיהיו בטוחים יותר אם ישמרו על מספר קטן ולא יקבלו יהודים נוספים, אך האחים בראשות טוביה החליטו להציל כמה שיותר יהודים.
claims.quote: many, many people within the Bielski group argued that they would be safer if they kept their numbers low and excluded other members from joining

claims.text: לפי USHMM, עד קיץ 1944 גדלה הקבוצה ל-1,200 איש, רובם קשישים, נשים וילדים.
claims.quote: By the summer of 1944, the group had grown to 1,200. The group consisted mainly of the elderly, women, and children.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, אסעאל היה סגנו של טוביה וזוס מונה לאחראי על סיור ומודיעין.
claims.quote: His brother Asael became his deputy, while Zus was placed in charge of reconnaissance.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, הוריהם ובני משפחה נוספים נהרגו בגטו באוגוסט 1941, וארבעת האחים נמלטו ליער.
claims.quote: after their parents and other family members were killed in the ghetto in August 1941

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בין יולי 1941 לסוף אביב 1942 הרגו השלטונות הגרמנים עשרות אלפי יהודים במחוז נובוגרודק, שכלל את הערים לידה ונובוגרודק.
claims.quote: German authorities killed tens of thousands of Jews in Nowogrodek (Novogrudok) District (including the cities of Lida and Nowogrodek) between July 1941 and the end of spring 1942.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בדצמבר 1943 עברה הקבוצה לבסיס קבע ביער נליבוקי.
claims.quote: the Bielski group moved in December 1943 to what became a permanent base in the Naliboki Forest

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בעת השחרור (קיץ 1944) הגיעה קבוצת ביילסקי לשיאה, 1,230 איש.
claims.quote: At the time of liberation, the Bielski group had reached its peak of 1,230 people.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, כ-50 מחברי הקבוצה נהרגו, שיעור אבדות נמוך במיוחד בהשוואה ליחידות פרטיזנים אחרות ולקבוצות יהודיות באזור.
claims.quote: An estimated 50 members of the Bielski group were killed, an unusually low casualty rate in comparison not only with other partisan detachments but also with Jewish groups in the region.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, כיום נחשבים פרטיזני ביילסקי לאחת מפעולות ההצלה הגדולות ביותר של יהודים בידי יהודים בהיסטוריית השואה.
claims.quote: Today, the Bielski partisans are considered one of the largest rescues of Jews by Jews in the history of the Holocaust.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, טוביה ביילסקי נולד ב-1906 בסטנקביץ' שבמערב בלארוס.
claims.quote: Tuvia Bielski was born in Stankiewicze, in western Belorussia, in 1906.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, משפחת ביילסקי הייתה משפחת איכרים יהודית בכפר סטנקביץ' והאחים הכירו היטב את האזור.
claims.quote: The Bielskis had been a Jewish farming family in the nearby village of Stankiewicze, and the brothers knew the region well.

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, טוביה הצטרף בגיל 17 לתנועת חלוצית ציונית, ב-1928 גויס לצבא הפולני והגיע לדרגת רב"ט.
claims.quote: At the age of seventeen he joined the Zionist pioneering movement, and in 1928 he was mobilized into the Polish army, where he rose to the rank of corporal.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בדצמבר 1941 רצחו הגרמנים בגטו נובוגרודק ארבעת אלפים יהודים, ובהם הוריהם של האחים.
claims.quote: in December of 1941, Germans descend onto the nearby Nowogródek ghetto, and murder four thousand Jews.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בני המשפחה בחרו בטוביה, איש צבא פולני לשעבר ופעיל ציוני, לפקד על הקבוצה.
claims.quote: The family members chose former Zionist activist Tuvia Bielski, a Polish Army veteran and a charismatic leader, to command the group.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בעזרת חברים בלארוסים לא יהודים הצליחו האחים להשיג נשק.
claims.quote: With the help of non-Jewish Belorussian friends, they were able to acquire guns.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, טוביה ראה בהצלת חיי יהודים אחיו את משימתו העיקרית.
claims.quote: Tuvia Bielski saw his principal mission as saving the lives of his fellow Jews.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, טוביה אמר ללוחמיו שיש להציל חיים ושהצלת יהודי חשובה בהרבה מהריגת גרמנים.
claims.quote: We have to save lives. To save a Jew is much more important than to kill Germans.

claims.text: לפי סרוגים, טוביה חזר ואמר לאנשיו שעדיף לו יהודי אחד חי מעשרה גרמנים מתים.
claims.quote: טוביה חזר ואמר לאנשיו עדיף לי עוד יהודי אחד חי מאשר עשרה גרמנים מתים.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, למרות התנגדות מסוימת בתוך הקבוצה טוביה לא הסס לקבל ולהגן על כל הפליטים היהודים, בלי קשר לגיל או למין.
claims.quote: Despite some opposition from within the group, Tuvia Bielski never wavered in his determination to accept and protect all Jewish refugees, regardless of age or gender.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, בסוף 1942 הצילה משימה מיוחדת יותר ממאה יהודים מגטו איווייה רגע לפני שהגרמנים תכננו לחסלו.
claims.quote: In late 1942, a special mission saved over a hundred Jews from the Iwie ghetto just as the Germans planned to liquidate it.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, משפחתו של קונסטנטין קוזלובסקי, שאינו יהודי, הסתירה יהודים שנמלטו מגטו נובוגרודק ופעלה עם הפרטיזנים לשחרר מאות יהודים מהגטו.
claims.quote: Many came through the family of Konstantin Kozlovski, a non-Jew, who provided shelter for Jews escaping from the Novogrudok ghetto

claims.text: לפי USHMM, זרם הניצולים היהודים הגדיל את הקבוצה לליותר מ-300 איש עד סוף 1942.
claims.quote: The stream of Jewish survivors increased the size of the Bielski group to more than 300 people by the end of 1942.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, עד פברואר 1943 חיו ביער 300 יהודים כפרטיזנים של ביילסקי.
claims.quote: By February of 1943, 300 Jews are living in the forest as Bielski partisans.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, באוגוסט 1943 החלו הגרמנים במצוד רחב נגד פרטיזנים רוסים, פולנים ויהודים באזור.
claims.quote: In August 1943, however, the Germans began a massive manhunt directed against Russian, Polish, and Jewish partisans in the region.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, הגרמנים הציעו פרס של 100,000 רייכסמארק תמורת מידע שיוביל ללכידת טוביה ביילסקי.
claims.quote: they offered a reward of 100,000 Reichmarks for information leading to Tuvia Bielski’s capture.

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, כשהורו לטוביה להשאיר רק לוחמים בודדים, הוא ידע שזה גזר דין מוות לאזרחים, סירב ופרש לעומק היער עם כל להקתו.
claims.quote: Bielski disobeyed, retreating to the thickest part of the forest with his entire band.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, הפרטיזנים שהו עשרה ימים מכוסי בוץ בביצה כשהם מתחמקים מסיורי גרמנים ומשתפי פעולה בלארוסים.
claims.quote: they spend ten days covered with mud, trying to evade the patrols of Germans and Belorussian collaborators that are hunting them.

claims.text: לפי סרוגים, גדודו של טוביה לא היה גדוד פרטיזנים רגיל אלא קהילה יהודית ביער, עם בית כנסת, בית דין, סדנאות, בית ספר ומרפאה.
claims.quote: גדודו לא היה גדוד פרטיזנים רגיל, אלא קהילה יהודית ביער, ובה בית-כנסת, בית-דין, סדנאות, בית-ספר, מרפאה.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, סדנאות המחנה, של סנדלרים, חייטים, נגרים, עובדי עור וצורפים, העסיקו לפחות 200 איש.
claims.quote: The group organized the skilled workers among the Jewish refugees into workshops, which employed at least 200 people, including cobblers, tailors, carpenters, leather workers, and blacksmiths.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, ביער נליבוקי פעלו בית חולים, כיתות לילדים, מפעל סבון, מרחץ טורקי, חייטים, קצבים וקבוצת נגנים שהופיעה בחגים.
claims.quote: There was a hospital, classrooms for the children, a soap factory, a Turkish bath, tailors, butchers, and even a group of musicians who played at festivals.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, ההנהגה ניהלה מרפאה פרימיטיבית, בית ספר לילדים, בית כנסת ואפילו בית דין וכלא.
claims.quote: The leadership managed a primitive infirmary, a school for the children, a synagogue, and even a courthouse/jail.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, במחנה נבנה בית ספר ליותר מ-50 ילדים.
claims.quote: Across the way, they construct a school for more than 50 children in the camp.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, למרות האנטישמיות בין יחידות סובייטיות, הגנרל "פלטון" הגן על קבוצת ביילסקי.
claims.quote: Despite the prevalence of antisemitic sentiment among several of the Soviet partisan detachments, General “Platon” protected the Bielski group.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, ביילסקי סירב לבקשות סובייטיות לספק יחידת מבצעים מבין כ-150 הגברים הלוחמים בקבוצתו.
claims.quote: Bielski refused Soviet requests to provide an operations unit from among the approximately 150 men in his group who engaged in armed operations.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, הקבוצה שיבשה רכבות גרמניות, פוצצה פסי רכבת והרסה גשרים, ועזרה לבריחות מגטאות יהודיים.
claims.quote: The group disabled German trains, blew up rail beds, destroyed bridges, and facilitated escapes from Jewish ghettos.

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, בקיץ 1944, עם שחרור האזור, צעדו ביילסקי ולהקת הפרטיזנים שלו, בת 1,230 איש, לעיר נובוגרודק.
claims.quote: In the summer of 1944, with the liberation of the area, Bielski and his 1,230-strong partisan band

claims.text: לפי USHMM, יותר מ-70 אחוז מחברי הקבוצה בשחרור היו נשים, קשישים וילדים שבלי הקבוצה היו אובדים תחת הכיבוש הגרמני.
claims.quote: More than 70 percent were women, elderly persons, and children, who otherwise would have perished under the German occupation.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, קבוצתו של טוביה הייתה הגדולה בקבוצות הפרטיזנים היהודיות.
claims.quote: Tuvia's group was the largest of the Jewish partisan groups.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, אחרי המלחמה חזרו ניצולים לבתים שנתפסו בידי מקומיים אנטישמים אלימים שסירבו להחזיר את רכושם.
claims.quote: the locals who now occupied the property that they had owned, were violently antisemitic and refused to give them quarter, or to discuss returning their property.

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, טוביה חזר אחרי המלחמה לפולין, ב-1945 עלה לפלשתינה וב-1954 התיישב בארצות הברית עם שני אחיו שנותרו בחיים.
claims.quote: After the war Bielski returned to Poland. That same year, in 1945, he immigrated to Palestine, and in 1954 he settled in the United States with his two surviving brothers.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, ב-1945 היגרו טוביה וזוס ביילסקי עם משפחותיהם לפלשתינה.
claims.quote: After World War II, in 1945 Tuvia and Zus Bielski emigrated with their families to Palestine.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, טוביה וזוס לחמו בכוחות המזוינים הישראליים במלחמת 1948 שהקימה את מדינת ישראל.
claims.quote: They both fought in the Israeli armed forces during the 1948 war that established the Israeli state.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, אחרי המלחמה עבדו טוביה וזוס בתחום התחבורה, בנהיגה במשאיות ובמוניות בניו יורק.
claims.quote: Tuvia and Zus each worked in transportation—driving trucks and taxis based out of New York.

claims.text: לפי סרוגים, אברהם ויינר, שעבד צמוד לטוביה, אמר שטוביה היה מלא כאב לאומי ואהבה לאומית ליהודים.
claims.quote: טוביה היה מלא על גדותיו כאב לאומי ואהבה לאומית ליהודים

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, איש מבני משפחת ביילסקי לא ביקש מעולם הכרה או פרס על מעשיו.
claims.quote: None of the Bielskis ever sought any recognition or reward for their actions.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, כשטוביה מת ב-1987 נקבר בלונג איילנד, ושנה אחר כך, לבקשת פרטיזנים ניצולים בישראל, הועלה ונקבר בהר המנוחות בירושלים בהלווית גיבור.
claims.quote: When Tuvia died in 1987, he was buried in Long Island, New York, but a year later, at the urging of surviving partisans in Israel, he was exhumed and given a hero's funeral at Har Hamenuchot, the hillside graveyard in Jerusalem.

claims.text: לפי סרוגים, שנה לאחר פטירת טוביה הועלתה גופתו ארצה והוא נקבר בהר המנוחות בטקס צבאי מלא.
claims.quote: שנה לאחר פטירתו גופתו הועלתה ארצה ונקבר בהר המנוחות בטקס צבאי מלא.

claims.text: לפי aboutholocaust, לפי הערכות מספר צאצאי קבוצת ביילסקי מגיע עד 10,000.
claims.quote: Some estimates place the number of descendants of the Bielski group as high as 10,000.

claims.text: לפי JPEF, ב-2008 הפך סיפורם של פרטיזני ביילסקי לסרט "עמידה" (Defiance) בכיכובם של דניאל קרייג וליב שרייבר.
claims.quote: In 2008 the inspiring story of the Bielski partisans was made into the motion picture Defiance, starring Daniel Craig and Liev Schreiber as Tuvia and Zus Bielski.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, סיפור פרטיזני ביילסקי הפך לסרט Defiance ב-2009.
claims.quote: The amazing story of the Bielski partisans was turned into the motion picture Defiance in 2009.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, הסרט Defiance יצא לאקרנים ב-16 בינואר 2009, זכה לביקורות מעורבות והעלה שאלות על תפקידן של קבוצות שונות במלחמה.
claims.quote: It opened to mixed reviews[22] and raised questions about the roles various groups played during the war.[23]

claims.text: לפי USHMM, הפרטיזנים שדדו לעיתים איכרים באיום נשק, ופעמים אחדות הרגו מי ששיתפו פעולה עם הגרמנים נגדם.
claims.quote: So sometimes they rob peasants at gunpoint. And a few times, they killed people who collaborated with the Germans against them.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, הקבוצה תקפה אנשי משטרה עזר בלארוסים ואיכרים מקומיים שנחשדו בהריגת יהודים.
claims.quote: It attacked the Belorussian auxiliary police officials, as well as local farmers suspected of killing Jews.

claims.text: לפי תיעוד פרטיזני שמצוטט ב-JewishGen, לוחמי שתי היחידות טענו שהרגו בסך הכול 381 לוחמי אויב.
claims.quote: According to partisan documentation, the Bielski fighters from both units claimed to have killed a total of 381 enemy fighters, sometimes during joint actions with Soviet groups.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, לוחמים לשעבר בבריגדה והיסטוריונים אחרים חולקים על כך וטוענים שהפרטיזנים הגיעו לאזור רק חודשים אחדים מאוחר יותר.
claims.quote: asserting that the partisans did not arrive in the area until several months later

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, המכון הפולני לזיכרון לאומי חוקר את הטבח מראשית שנות ה-2000, ועד אפריל 2009 לא פרסם ממצאים רשמיים.
claims.quote: The Polish Institute of National Remembrance has been investigating the massacre since the early 2000s. As of April 2009, it has not issued official findings.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, חלק מהפרטיזנים חשבו שהאחים שתלטנים, אך טוביה ראה במשמעת תנאי להישרדות הקבוצה.
claims.quote: Some partisans think the brothers are overbearing. But Tuvia sees discipline as essential to the group’s survival.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, יש תיאורים המציינים אי שוויון בין פרטיזנים אמידים לתושבים עניים במחנה.
claims.quote: Some accounts note the inequality between well-off partisans and poor inhabitants of the camp.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, אחרי כניסת הסובייטים חקרה ה-NKVD את האחים על שמועות לגבי שלל שאספו במלחמה.
claims.quote: The NKVD started interrogating the Bielski brothers about the rumors of loot they had reportedly collected during the war

claims.text: לפי ביוגרפיה באוספי USHMM, ארבעת האחים שנותרו נמלטו ליער יחד עם 13 אחרים.
claims.quote: the four surviving Bielski brothers fled to the nearby forest along with 13 others

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, האחים יצרו ביער גרעין פרטיזני של 17 חברים, רובם בני משפחת ביילסקי.
claims.quote: they created a seventeen-member partisan core there, consisting mostly of members of Bielski's family.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, הקבוצה מנתה בתחילה כארבעים איש וצמחה במהירות.
claims.quote: Originally, the group consisted of around forty people, but grew quickly.

claims.text: לפי USHMM, אסעאל גויס לצבא האדום ומת בחזית במזרח פרוסיה בפברואר 1945.
claims.quote: Asael was drafted into the Soviet Army. He died on the front in East Prussia in February 1945.

claims.text: לפי כיתוב תמונה באוספי USHMM, אסעאל ביילסקי נהרג בקרב קניגסברג ב-1944 כשלחם בצבא האדום.
claims.quote: Asael Bielski was killed during the battle of Koenigsberg in 1944 while fighting in the Red Army.

claims.text: לפי יד ושם, אסעאל ביילסקי נהרג בקרב כחייל בצבא הסובייטי בקניגסברג ב-1944.
claims.quote: Asael Bielski was killed in battle as a soldier in the Soviet army at Konigsberg in 1944.

claims.text: לפי aboutholocaust, אסעאל נהרג בינואר 1945 אחרי שגויס לצבא האדום.
claims.quote: Asael was killed in January 1945 after being conscripted into the Red Army.

claims.text: האנציקלופדיה של USHMM: בדצמבר 1943, לבסיס קבע ביער
claims.quote: the Bielski group moved in December 1943 to what became a permanent base in the Naliboki Forest
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: הפודקאסט של USHMM: בקיץ 1943, לפני המצוד הגרמני, הוביל טוביה את הקבוצה ליער נליבוקי
claims.quote: take the group to the Naliboki Forest, nearly 20 miles away
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: יד ושם: כבר בקיץ 1943 ערכו הגרמנים מצוד ביער נליבוקי, בין השאר נגד קבוצת ביילסקי
claims.quote: In the summer of 1943, the Germans initiated a massive hunt through the Naliboki Forest
claims.checker_note: audit: page could not be fetched by script; verifier quoted it

claims.text: aboutholocaust: באוגוסט 1943 נאלצה הקבוצה להקים מחנה בעומק יער נליבוקי
claims.quote: In August 1943, the group was forced to make camp deep in the Naliboki Forest
claims.checker_note: audit: quote found on the fetched page

claims.text: טוביה ביילסקי ואחיו, משפחת איכרים יהודית מסביבת נובוגרודק, הובילו את פרטיזני ביילסקי, שסיפורם הפך לסרט "עמידה" (Defiance) בכיכובם של דניאל קרייג וליב שרייבר.
claims.quote: The Bielskis had been a Jewish farming family in the nearby village of Stankiewicze, and the brothers knew the region well.

claims.text: טוביה ביילסקי ואחיו, משפחת איכרים יהודית מסביבת נובוגרודק, הובילו את פרטיזני ביילסקי, שסיפורם הפך לסרט "עמידה" (Defiance) בכיכובם של דניאל קרייג וליב שרייבר.
claims.quote: a family of Polish Jews who led the organization.

claims.text: בשיא: בין 1,200 ל-1,236 איש
claims.quote: at its peak, 1,236 people belonged to the group, and 70% were women, children, and the elderly; no one was turned away.

claims.text: בשיא: בין 1,200 ל-1,236 איש
claims.quote: At the time of liberation, the Bielski group had reached its peak of 1,230 people.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, שמע הסדנאות הגיע לפרטיזנים הרחק מבסיס ביילסקי.
claims.quote: More than 125 workers toiled in the workshops, which became famous among partisans far beyond the Bielski base.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, איש לא נדחה.
claims.quote: at its peak, 1,236 people belonged to the group, and 70% were women, children, and the elderly; no one was turned away.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, בדומה לקבוצות פרטיזנים אחרות בסביבה, אנשי ביילסקי פשטו על כפרים ולקחו מזון בכוח.
claims.quote: Like other partisan groups in the area, the Bielski group would raid nearby villages and forcibly seize food;

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, לעיתים סבלו איכרים שסירבו לחלוק את המזון מאלימות ואף נרצחו.
claims.quote: on occasion, peasants who refused to share their food with the partisans were the subject of violence and even murder.

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, חלק מחברי היחידה, אך לא האחים עצמם, הואשמו בפשעי מלחמה.
claims.quote: Some of the members of the Bielski partisans (but not the Bielski brothers themselves) have been accused of war crimes

claims.text: לפי JewishGen, בין היתר הואשמו בהשתתפות לכאורה בטבח נליבוקי ב-1943, שבו הרגו פרטיזנים סובייטים 129 איש.
claims.quote: on the neighbouring population, particularly for alleged involvement in the 1943 Naliboki massacre of 129 people

claims.text: JewishGen: יותר מ-125 עובדים
claims.quote: More than 125 workers toiled in the workshops, which became famous among partisans far beyond the Bielski base.

claims.text: JewishGen: 1,236 איש
claims.quote: at its peak, 1,236 people belonged to the group, and 70% were women, children, and the elderly

An introduction by the JewishPartisans organization to the story of the brothers Tuvia, Asael, Zus and Aron Bielski, who turned their family's struggle for survival into an organized Jewish partisan community.
Aron Bielski, the last of the brothers, speaks in a USC Shoah Foundation testimony at the places where the remembered partisan activity took place.
Tamara Vershitskaya, researcher and founder of the Museum of Jewish Resistance in Novogrudok, presents the history of the Bielski Jewish partisan unit in the Naliboki Forest.
Walking among overgrown trenches at the site of the former Bielski brothers' camp in the Naliboki Forest.

quote_translations.c66: Tuvia told his men again and again: I would rather have one more living Jew than ten dead Germans.
quote_translations.c67: His battalion was not an ordinary partisan battalion, but a Jewish community in the forest, with a synagogue, a court, workshops, a school, a clinic.
quote_translations.c68: Tuvia was overflowing with national pain and national love for the Jews
quote_translations.c50: A year after his death his body was brought to Israel and he was buried at Har Hamenuchot in a full military ceremony.
